messages.author: d872209dd5f34bd5
messages.subject: Scenario change
parts:
Hi all, 

I am managing to run the ectotherm model with micro_era5, but would like to change the scenario to identify changes in my organisms activity. When I do change this, I receive the following error -

error: maxshades must be a vector with a length equal to the number of days simulated 
error: minshades must be a vector with a length equal to the number of days simulated

I have noticed others with the same error on this forum, but they are usually changing parameters in the microclimate model which I am not. The only thing I change is the scenario (scenario = 2), everything else is set to default. Then when the ectotherm model is run the above errors occur.
I have looked the number of days min/max are calculated for, with both being the same length as days simulated. I have specified minshades <- micro$minshade and
maxshades <- micro$maxshade in the ectotherm model which returns the same error. I have run the default micro_ncep which returns results with the ectotherm model, but with the scenario change it returns the same error.

Does anyone have any suggestions as to what I'm overlooking here? 

Thank you, 

Shane

messages.subject: Re: Scenario change
parts:
Hi Shane,
Try simulating full years rather than partial years - I think that's the problem. I'll look into making it work for partial years.
Note also you should in general run about one year as a 'spin up' to remove the initial conditions (esp. soil moisture effects but also snow effects).
All the best,
Mike

messages.author: 2bcecdd9c0443e65
messages.subject: Re: Scenario change
parts:
Quick note, Shane: looking at your spatial extent, the ERA5 netCDF downloaded via request_era5 for one year shouldn't be much more than ~20 MB. If it's significantly bigger than that, do let me know (I'm the maintainer for the mcera5 package, which includes request_era5).

Perhaps, you may have received a timeout error upon attempting to download a full year. If so, this doesn't have much to do with how large the download request is, as it does the global usage of the ECMWF Climate Data Store API by other people at the time of your request. As a result download times can be stochastic – sometimes a file may take hours, another day the same file only a few minutes.

Best,
Dave

messages.author: 2bcecdd9c0443e65
messages.subject: Re: Scenario change
parts:
Hi Shane,

Thanks for bringing this to my attention. I was surprised you were facing this error about your request having too many fields: for years the limit for ERA5 has been 120,000 fields, and yet your error says the limit is 60,000. A 120,000 for ERA5 hourly single levels is still what the ECMWF documentation Confluence says (see Table 2 here).

But after some digging, I see that in a blog post, the limit for ERA5 just changed from 120,000 to 60,000 in early April, albeit this change should only be temporary:
https://forum.ecmwf.int/t/a-new-cds-soon-to-be-launched-expect-some-disruptions/1607

As for why the number of fields (105120) may have remained the same even though you shrank the spatial extent: given the large grid cell size of ERA5 (0.25 x 0.25), and the rounding of grid coordinates that request_era5() does under the hood, you sometimes need to decrease the extent considerably in order to change the number of fields. But, it's changing the temporal duration that really does any good in changing # of fields: 12 ERA5 variables x 8,760 hourly timesteps = many fields that stack up over time.

So the request you outline above should work in its entirety, but for the time being you'll need to be flexible with the temporary lower field limit. But regardless, as we suggest in our mcera5 paper, and also stated in that blog post, the CDS requests will indeed be much more efficient if you request a shorter temporal duration, as Shane did here, and then combine the netCDF files together. Seeing this (albeit temporary) lower limit of 60,000, I might change the combine = TRUE feature in `request_era5()` so that it's easier to combine months rather than just years...will work on this soon!

Cheers,
Dave

Hi Dave, 

Thank you for the reply! This made the issues at hand very clear.

I have since successfully downloaded 2 lots of 6 months (January - June and July - December) for my spatial extent, then combined the two NC files together to represent the full year, as suggested. 

Using the combined NC file, the ectotherm model successfully ran with and without the scenario change function (as suggested by Mike earlier in this thread). The original error regarding minshades and maxshades never occurred when using the scenario function with the combined 'full year' NC file.

Everything seems to be working fine! 

Thank you both for your help and insight, 

Shane
